q: In Zechariah 14, what will the LORD withhold from the families of the earth that do not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King?
a: Rain

q: In Zechariah 14, which nation is named specifically as facing a plague if its people will not go up to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles?
a: Egypt

q: In Zechariah 14, what will be inscribed on the bells of the horses on that day?
a: HOLY TO THE LORD

q: Is the book of Malachi found in the Old Testament or the New Testament?
a: Old Testament

q: Which of these best describes the book of Malachi?
a: Minor Prophet

q: In Malachi 1:2-3, which brother does the LORD say He has loved, and which brother does He say He has hated?
a: He loved Jacob and hated Esau

q: In Malachi 1:4, what do the people of Edom say they will do after being devastated, and how does the LORD of Hosts respond?
a: They will rebuild the ruins; the LORD says He will demolish

q: In Malachi 1:6-7, how does the LORD say the priests have despised His name?
a: By presenting defiled food on His altar

q: In Malachi 1:8, the LORD says offering blind and lame animals is wrong and tells the priests to try offering them to whom?
a: Their governor

q: In Malachi 1:11, the LORD says His name will be great among whom, from where the sun rises to where it sets?
a: The nations

q: In Malachi 2, what did the LORD say He would do to the priests if they did not take it to heart to honor His name?
a: Send a curse among them and curse their blessings

q: In Malachi 2, why did the LORD say the lips of a priest should preserve knowledge and people should seek instruction from his mouth?
a: Because he is the messenger of the LORD of Hosts

q: In Malachi 2:13, what did the people do to the altar of the LORD because He no longer regarded their offerings?
a: They covered it with tears, weeping and groaning

q: In Malachi 3:1, what does the LORD of Hosts say He will send to prepare the way before Him?
a: My messenger

q: In Malachi 3:2, what two things is the coming Lord compared to, as He purifies His people?
a: A refiner’s fire and a launderer’s soap

q: In Malachi 3:3, whom will the Lord purify and refine like gold and silver so that they present offerings in righteousness?
a: The sons of Levi

q: In Malachi 3:6, what reason does the LORD give for why the descendants of Jacob have not been destroyed?
a: The LORD does not change

q: In Malachi 3:10, the LORD says, "Bring the full tithe into the storehouse," and promises what if His people test Him in this?
a: Open the windows of heaven and pour out blessing without measure

q: In Malachi 3, the people complained that serving God was futile. Whom did they say they now call blessed?
a: The arrogant

q: In Malachi 3:16, a scroll of remembrance was written before the LORD regarding which people?
a: Those who feared the LORD and honored His name

q: In the book of Malachi, what did the people who feared the LORD do?
a: They spoke with one another

q: What was written before the LORD about the people who feared Him?
a: A scroll of remembrance

q: In Malachi 3, to what does the LORD compare how He will spare those who fear Him?
a: A man sparing his own son who serves him

q: In the book of Malachi, the LORD said His people would again see the difference between which two groups?
a: Those who serve God and those who do not

q: In Malachi 4:2, what will rise with healing in its wings for those who fear the LORD's name?
a: The sun of righteousness

q: In the book of Malachi, God promised to send Elijah the prophet. Whose hearts would Elijah turn to their children?
a: The hearts of the fathers

q: Why is it added, And sits at the right hand of God?
a: Christ ascended to manifest Himself as Head of His Church, through whom the Father governs all things.

q: According to Matthew's genealogy, Jesus is described as the son of David and the son of whom?
a: Abraham

q: How will the world end?
a: Jesus will return personally and visibly in glory, raise the dead, and judge all people

q: Every good gift comes from God, and Jesus said God can destroy both body and soul in hell. How should we feel toward God?
a: Love him and fear him too

q: Name the five stages of Christ's humiliation.
a: Conceived by the Holy Spirit, suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, dead, and buried

q: What did Joseph want to do when he discovered Mary was pregnant?
a: Divorce her quietly

q: Why was it requisite that the Mediator should be God and man in one person?
a: So the works of His divine and human natures are accepted by God for us.

q: What was special about Jesus’ mother?
a: She was a virgin

q: How did Christ, being the Son of God, become man?
a: Christ took a true body and soul, conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of Mary

q: Why was it requisite that the Mediator should be God?
a: God's Mediator must be God to sustain human nature under wrath, give worth to His sacrifice, satisfy justice, and bring salvation.

q: Are there not also evil angels?
a: Yes; evil angels fell through pride and disobedience, forever excluded from God. The devil is their king

q: What three aspects of God's will are mentioned in the lesson?
a: That we believe the Gospel and be saved, obey His commandments and be holy, willingly submit to His dealings.

q: What did they find in Bethlehem?
a: The little child and his mother

q: Until when did Jesus remain in Egypt with his parents, when he was a baby?
a: Until the death of Herod the Great

q: Children in the region of what age were to be killed, in the hope that the young Jesus would also be killed?
a: Two years and under

q: Which ruler ordered the massacre of infant boys in Bethlehem after Jesus was born?
a: Herod

q: When King Herod was angry, whom did he try to harm in Bethlehem?
a: The little boys of Bethlehem

q: In Matthew 2, Archelaus was ruling Judea when the holy family returned from Egypt; who was his father?
a: Herod

q: According to Matthew 2:22, who was reigning in Judea in place of his father Herod?
a: Archelaus

q: To whom is Baptism to be administered?
a: To all who actually profess repentance toward God and faith in Christ.

q: How is Baptism rightly administered?
a: By immersion or dipping the whole body in water according to Christ's institution.

q: What do you need to know in order to live and die in the joy of this comfort?
a: How great my sins and misery are; how I am delivered from them; how to be thankful

q: Since then faith alone makes us share in Christ and all His benefits, where does this faith come from?
a: From the Holy Spirit, who works it by the gospel and strengthens it through the sacraments.

q: What are the parts of a sacrament?
a: Two parts: an outward sensible sign according to Christ's appointment, and an inward spiritual grace signified thereby

q: How do they that worthily communicate in the Lord's supper feed upon the body and blood of Christ therein?
a: Spiritually, not carnally, present to faith; truly and really receiving Christ crucified and his benefits

q: Where did the people who went out to John the Baptist come from?
a: Jerusalem, Judea, and around the Jordan

q: Who went to hear John preach?
a: All the people of the land

q: While John was baptizing, what did he call the Pharisees and Sadducees?
a: Brood of vipers

q: How is Christ to be exalted in his coming again to judge the world?
a: Christ shall come at the last day in great power and glory, with His holy angels, to judge the world in righteousness.
ref: Acts 3:14-15; Matt 24:30; Luke 9:26; Matt 25:31; 1 Thess 4:16; Acts 17:31

q: What did Jesus answer when John tried to stop Him from being baptized?
a: "Let it be so now."

q: What does the Bible say about hatred?
a: Hatred of one's brother is murder in the heart.

q: How do Baptism and the Lord's Supper, become effectual Means of Salvation?
a: Not from virtue in them or the minister, but by Christ's blessing.

q: In what three ways does God grant answers to our prayers?
a: By granting what we ask (perhaps after delay), giving good instead of harmful things, or giving strength to bear burdens.

q: After His temptation, in which town by the sea did Jesus go to live?
a: Capernaum

q: After Jesus answered the devil about the bread, where did the devil take Him, as Matthew tells it?
a: To Jerusalem, the holy city

q: What Bible words did the devil say to get Jesus to jump?
a: "He will command His angels concerning You"

q: For whom does God care most?
a: For man; and especially for His believing children

q: What does our Lord say in Matthew 4:10?
a: Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.

q: After John the Baptist was put in prison, to what part of the land did Jesus go?
a: To Galilee

q: Where did Jesus preach during the second year of his teaching?
a: In Galilee

q: When Jesus left Nazareth and began his ministry in Capernaum, what message did he preach?
a: Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near

q: Which town by the Sea of Galilee served as the base for much of Jesus' ministry?
a: Capernaum

q: To what place did Jesus go from Nazareth?
a: To Capernaum by the sea

q: Where did he live while he preached in Galilee?
a: At Capernaum

q: Which book of the Bible contains the 'Sermon on the Mount'?
a: Matthew

q: Wherein consists the sinfulness of that Estate whereinto Man fell?
a: Guilt of Adam's Sin, want of Original Righteousness, Corruption of Nature, and all actual Transgressions

q: What shall be done to the Wicked at the Day of Judgment?
a: Bodies raised and sentenced with their Souls to unspeakable Torments with the Devil and his Angels forever

q: Does God in this commandment forbid nothing more than adultery and similar shameful sins?
a: Since we are temples of the Holy Spirit, God forbids all unchaste acts, words, thoughts, desires, and whatever entices us to unchastity.

q: What hath God especially decreed concerning angels and men?
a: God eternally elected some angels to glory and some men to eternal life in Christ, and foreordained others to wrath.

q: May any who profess the faith, and desire to come to the Lord's supper, be kept from it?
a: Yes; the ignorant and scandalous are to be excluded by church power until reformed

q: In Matthew 5:1, what did Jesus do when He saw the crowds?
a: He went up on the mountain and sat down

q: In Matthew 5:3-10, how many "Blessed are..." statements (the Beatitudes) does Jesus speak in the Sermon on the Mount?
What rule has God given for our direction in prayer?
a: The whole Word of God directs us in prayer; especially the Lord's Prayer.

q: In Matthew 5:17, what did Jesus say he came to do to the Law and the Prophets?
a: To fulfill them, not to abolish them

q: What is the relation between the Old and New Testaments?
a: The Old Testament prepared the way for the New; the New Testament fulfills the Old and completes God's revelation.

q: Jesus said that anyone who says to his brother, 'You fool!' will face what?
a: The fire of hell

q: In Matthew 5:28, what has a man already done if he looks at a woman with lust?
a: He has already committed adultery with her in his heart

q: What shall immediately follow after the resurrection?
a: General and final judgment of angels and men; day and hour unknown, so all watch and pray

q: Jesus said it is better to lose one part of your body than for what to happen?
a: For your whole body to go to hell

q: In the Sermon on the Mount, what did Jesus say a man commits if he marries a divorced woman?
a: Adultery

q: Under what condition only may a divorce be obtained?
a: Only if one party is guilty of adultery; then the innocent party may obtain a divorce.

q: What did Jesus say about swearing an oath to make a promise?
a: Do not swear at all

q: In the Sermon on the Mount, what does Jesus tell us the earth is?
a: God’s footstool

q: Jesus said not to “swear by your head” because you cannot do what?
a: Make one hair black or white

q: What did Jesus say you should do if someone forces you to go one mile?
a: Go with them two miles

q: Does God give daily bread to those only who pray for it?
a: No; He gives daily bread also to the wicked, but they receive it without thanksgiving, and miss His blessing

q: Why does God give daily bread even to the wicked?
a: God is good and seeks to lead all men to repentance through His goodness.

q: Jesus said, "Be ___, as your heavenly Father is ___." What is the missing word?
a: Perfect

q: What does our Savior say in Matthew 5:48?
a: Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.

q: Since we have been delivered from our misery by grace alone through Christ, without any merit of our own, why must we yet do good works?
a: Show thankfulness to God and praise Him; assure ourselves of faith by its fruits; win neighbors to Christ by godly living.

q: How is the Lord's prayer to be used?
a: As pattern for other prayers and as prayer itself, with understanding, faith, reverence, and other necessary graces

q: In Matthew 6, what does Jesus say will happen if you perform your righteous acts before men to be seen by them?
a: You will have no reward from your Father in heaven

q: How many of Jesus’ brothers are named in the Bible?
a: Four

q: Which list gives the names of Jesus’ brothers?
a: James, Joses, Judas, and Simon

q: Where did the hypocrites “love to pray”?
a: Standing in synagogues and on street corners

q: Where in the Bible can you find the Lord’s Prayer?
a: Matthew 6

q: In how many places in the Gospels is the Lord's Prayer given?
a: Two

q: What does the Preface of the Lord's Prayer teach us?
a: To approach God with reverence and confidence as children to a Father, and to pray with and for others

q: When is the name of God hallowed among us?
a: When God's Word is taught purely and we lead holy lives by it

q: What gifts do we ask God for in the first three petitions of the Lord's Prayer?
a: Heavenly gifts—that His name be hallowed, His kingdom come, and His will be done

q: Why does Christ teach us to pray first for His heavenly gifts?
a: Because we most urgently need them for our salvation and eternal welfare

q: What can be said about the structure of the seven petitions?
a: First three concern God's glory (Name, Kingdom, Will); last four our needs. Six are spiritual, one temporal.

q: In the First Petition of the Lord's Prayer, "Hallowed be Your name," how should we understand what 'God's name' means?
a: Not only the names by which we address Him, but all the ways He is known to us.

q: How many petitions are there in the Lord's Prayer?
a: Six.

q: Of how many parts doth the Lord's prayer consist?
a: Three parts: a preface, petitions, and a conclusion

q: What is meant by saying that the kingdom of God comes to us?
a: It means that we become partakers in it

q: What three actions do we ask God to take regarding His will?
a: Frustrate the will of the devil, world, and flesh; strengthen us to overcome them; keep us steadfast in faith.

q: What do we pray for in the second petition?
a: That the gospel may be preached in all the world and believed and obeyed by all

q: Why is the word "today" added?
a: So that I should not be anxious for tomorrow, but let each day bear its own burdens

q: In the Fourth Petition, "Give us this day our daily bread," what do we pray that God would lead us to do?
a: To realize that God gives daily bread even to the wicked, and to receive it with thanksgiving

q: How are the forgiveness petition and the daily bread petition closely connected?
a: Daily forgiveness of sins is as necessary for souls as daily bread is for bodies.

q: What is implied by the word "debts"?
a: Thereby is implied our guilt or debt to God, which we have brought upon ourselves by our sins

q: What three things do we accomplish in the petition about forgiveness?
a: We acknowledge our sinfulness, pray for forgiveness, and promise to forgive others.

q: What does the prayer for forgiveness presuppose about our state of heart?
a: A penitent state of heart; without true penitence, the petition becomes mockery.

q: On what ground do we ask God for forgiveness in this petition?
a: We pray believing God will be gracious and merciful to us for Jesus' sake.

q: In the Fifth Petition ("forgive us our debts"), what do we pray our Father in heaven will not do?
a: Look upon our sins, or deny our prayer on account of them.

q: When temptations assail us, what do we pray our Father to do?
a: Keep us steadfast, strengthen us to fight the good fight of faith, and preserve us in true faith.

q: In the Sixth Petition, how do the devil, the world, and our flesh try to deceive us?
a: They promise happiness in sin's paths while such paths lead only to misery and destruction.

q: What connection exists between the sixth and seventh petitions?
a: Sixth seeks preservation from sin; seventh seeks deliverance from evil resulting from sin.

q: According to the catechism, what do we pray in the seventh petition, as in a summary?
a: That our Father in heaven would deliver us from every evil of body and soul, property and honor, and grant a blessed end.

q: From what kinds of evils do we suffer in this world?
a: Evils affecting body (sickness, pain), soul (sin, unbelief), property (poverty), character (disgrace).

q: How do we pray for deliverance from evil in this world?
a: Ward off affliction when possible, give grace to bear it patiently, remove what distresses us.

q: Right after the prayer, Jesus talked about forgiving others. What did He say happens if we do not forgive others?
a: Your Father will not forgive your sins either

q: In the Sermon on the Mount, what does Jesus say you should do when you fast?
a: Anoint your head and wash your face

q: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus says the hypocrites who disfigure their faces when they fast already have what?
a: Their full reward

q: What happens to “treasures on earth”?
a: Moth and rust destroy them, and thieves break in and steal them

q: What is your only comfort in life and death?
a: I belong to Jesus Christ who paid for all my sins and ensures all things work for my salvation

q: What does our Lord teach us by placing daily bread after the petitions for heavenly gifts?
a: That heavenly gifts for our soul are much more important than earthly provision for our body

q: If a poor Creature comes to Christ, crying, lamenting and confessing his sins, will Christ receive him?
a: YES, YES: His merciful Arms are spread wide open to receive him

q: Are all men, then, saved by Christ just as they perished through Adam?
a: No. Only those are saved who by a true faith are grafted into Christ and accept all His benefits.

q: What is required in the seventh Commandment?
a: Requireth preservation of our own and our neighbor's chastity in heart, speech, and behavior.

q: In Matthew 7:6, what does Jesus say not to throw before swine?
a: Pearls

q: In which book of the New Testament is the following passage found: "Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you"? (Hint: it is part of the Sermon on the Mount.)
a: Matthew

q: Does this teaching not make people careless and wicked?
a: No. It is impossible that those grafted into Christ by true faith should not bring forth fruits of thankfulness.

q: Why were the crowds astonished at Jesus' teaching at the end of the Sermon on the Mount?
a: He taught as one who had authority, and not as their scribes

q: In Mark 8:9, about how many men did Jesus feed in the region of Decapolis at one time?
a: To four thousand men

q: In Matthew 8:3, after Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man with leprosy, what did He say?
a: “I am willing. Be clean!”

q: In which town did a centurion plead with Jesus to heal his paralyzed servant, whom Jesus healed without going to him?
a: Capernaum

q: Which Roman centurion asked Jesus to heal his servant, saying he was not worthy for Jesus to come under his roof?
a: A centurion in Capernaum

q: What did Jesus say there will be in the outer darkness?
a: Crying and grinding teeth

q: According to Matthew 8:17, Jesus fulfilled the prophecy that He took on our infirmities and carried what?
a: Our diseases

q: After Jesus healed the demon-possessed men on the other side of the sea and crossed back by boat, to which town did he come (Matt 9:1)?
a: To his own town, Capernaum

q: In Matthew 8, after the herd of pigs drowned in the sea, how did the whole town respond when they saw Jesus?
a: They begged Him to leave their region

q: May we also swear by saints or other creatures?
a: No. Lawful oath calls upon God alone, who knows our heart, to witness truth. No creature deserves such honour.

q: In Matthew 9, who came to Jesus asking why they and the Pharisees fasted often while His disciples did not?
a: John’s disciples

q: When John’s disciples asked Jesus about fasting, whom did Jesus say would be taken away, after which His disciples would fast?
a: The bridegroom

q: In Jesus' teaching in Matthew 9, what happens if someone sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment?
a: The patch pulls away and a worse tear results

q: In Jesus' teaching in Matthew 9, what do people do with new wine so that both the wine and the containers are preserved?
a: They pour it into new wineskins

q: Which woman was healed after coming up behind Jesus in a crowd and touching the fringe of His cloak?
a: The woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years

q: What did the woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years touch in order to be healed?
a: The fringe of Jesus' cloak

q: After the two blind men came to Jesus in the house, what did Jesus ask them before healing them?
a: "Do you believe that I am able to do this?"

q: After Jesus healed the two blind men, how did the man with a demon who could not talk get to Jesus?
a: Someone brought him to Jesus.

q: How does the second petition relate to Christian missionary work?
a: It is a prayer for missions; if sincere, we must give liberally so the Gospel may be preached to all.

q: In Matthew 10:1, Jesus called his twelve disciples to him and gave them authority over what?
a: Unclean spirits

q: What did Jesus do in Perea, the region beyond the Jordan?
a: He went through the land teaching

q: In Matthew 10:2-3, which apostle named James is described as the brother of John?
a: James son of Zebedee

q: In Matthew 10:3, which apostle is named right after Philip in the list of the twelve?
a: Bartholomew

q: In Matthew 10:2-4, which apostle is named right after James son of Alphaeus?
a: Thaddaeus

q: In Matthew 10:3, the apostle James listed next to Thaddaeus is called the son of whom?
a: Alphaeus

q: Which of the Twelve, listed in Matthew 10:3, is traditionally called "James the Less" to distinguish him from James the brother of John?
a: James son of Alphaeus

q: Jesus initially sent the twelve disciples to preach to which group of people?
a: The lost sheep of Israel

q: What proof do we have that it is right to baptize little children?
a: Christ said, 'Let the little children come to Me.' Children are included in 'all nations.'

q: When Jesus warned His disciples they would be handed over for trial, who did He say would speak through them?
a: The Spirit of your Father

q: Why didn't Jesus' disciples need to worry about what to say when they were handed over?
a: The Spirit of their Father would speak through them

q: According to Jesus in Matthew 10:22, who will be saved?
a: The one who perseveres to the end

q: Who, then, receive this sacrament worthily?
a: Those who have faith in the words, "This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins."

q: In Matthew 10, besides loving Him more than family, what does Jesus say a person must do to be worthy of Him?
a: Take up his cross and follow Me

q: How hath Christ appointed bread and wine to be given and received in the sacrament of the Lord's supper?
a: Ministers set apart bread and wine by word of institution, thanksgiving, and prayer; give to communicants who eat and drink

q: What did Jesus say of John the Baptist when John's disciples came to Him from prison?
a: Among those born of women there has risen no one greater than John the Baptist.

q: What do the scriptures make known of God?
a: The scriptures make known what God is, the persons in the Godhead, his decrees, and the execution of them.

q: When does the kingdom of God come to us?
a: When the Father gives us His Holy Spirit, so we believe His Word and live a godly life

q: In Matthew 11:14, Jesus said John the Baptist is which prophet who was to come?
a: Elijah

q: In Jesus' words about John in Matthew 11, what did people say about John because he came neither eating nor drinking?
a: “He has a demon!”

q: Why did Jesus begin to denounce the cities where most of His miracles had been performed?
a: Because they did not repent

q: Which cities did Jesus speak against because they did not turn from their sins after seeing His miracles?
a: Chorazin, Bethsaida, and Capernaum

q: In Matthew 11, Jesus said it would be more bearable on the day of judgment for which city than for Capernaum?
a: Sodom

q: What did Jesus say about Capernaum and the day of judgment?
a: Sodom would have it easier than Capernaum

q: Are all they saved who hear the gospel, and live in the church?
a: Not all who hear the gospel and live in the visible church are saved, but only true members of the invisible church.

q: When the Pharisees complained about the disciples picking grain, what story did Jesus remind them of?
a: What David did when he was hungry

q: When the Pharisees criticized His disciples for picking grain on the Sabbath, what did Jesus say is "Lord of the Sabbath"?
a: The Son of Man

q: In which miracle of Jesus, in a synagogue, did people ask Him, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”
a: Healing the man with the withered hand

q: When Jesus withdrew after the Pharisees plotted to kill Him, and He healed all the large crowds that followed Him, what did He warn those crowds?
a: Not to make Him known

q: In Matthew 12, what kind of man was brought to Jesus?
a: A blind man with a demon who could not talk

q: What did the crowds ask when Jesus healed the man who was blind and could not speak?
a: Could this be the Son of David?

q: When Jesus answered the Pharisees who accused Him of driving out demons by Beelzebul, what did He say would happen to every kingdom divided against itself?
a: It will be laid waste

q: Why was it so wrong for the Pharisees to say Jesus drove out demons by Beelzebul?
a: They said the Spirit's work was the devil's

q: After the Pharisees said Jesus drove out demons by Beelzebul, what sin did Jesus warn would not be forgiven?
a: Speaking against the Holy Spirit

q: In Matthew 12:32, what does Jesus say will happen to whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man?
a: He will be forgiven

q: In Matthew 12, Jesus says that speaking against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven in which time periods?
a: Either in this age or in the one to come

q: What did Jesus say people will do on the day of judgment for every careless word they have spoken?
a: Give an account for them

q: How is God's name taken in vain thoughtlessly?
a: By using it as an exclamation, reading God's Word without devotion, jesting about sacred things, and quoting Scripture in fun.

q: When some scribes and Pharisees asked Jesus for a sign, who did Jesus say would rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom?
a: The Queen of the South

q: In Jesus' teaching about the unclean spirit that leaves a man, what condition does the spirit find the house in when it returns?
a: Vacant, swept clean, and put in order

q: In Jesus' teaching about an unclean spirit that comes out of a man, how many other spirits does it bring back with it?
a: Seven other spirits

q: When the disciples asked Jesus why he spoke to the people in parables, what did he say had been given to the disciples but not to the crowds?
a: The knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven

q: When will our lives be decent and modest?
a: When our hearts are chaste and pure from evil lusts and unclean thoughts.

q: In the parable of the sower, what did the seed that fell among thorns represent?
a: Those hearing God's word but choked by worldly cares

q: In Matthew 13, which parable did Jesus tell right after the parable of the Sower?
a: The parable of the Wheat and the Weeds

q: According to Matthew 13, what did Jesus' speaking in parables fulfill, as spoken through the prophet?
a: "I will utter things hidden since the foundation of the world."

q: In Jesus' story of the weeds, who is the one who sows the good seed?
a: The Son of Man

q: In Jesus' story of the weeds, what does the good seed stand for?
a: The sons of the kingdom

q: In Jesus' story of the weeds, what do the weeds stand for?
a: The sons of the evil one

q: In Jesus' explanation of the parable of the weeds, who are the harvesters at the end of the age?
a: Angels

q: Who are the enemies of the church?
a: The enemies of the church are the devil, the world, and our own flesh. Its last enemy is death.

q: Jesus said that at the end of the age He will send out His angels. What will they do?
a: Throw all who do evil into the fire

q: In Matthew 13, which parable of the kingdom of heaven ends with angels separating the wicked from the righteous at the end of the age?
a: The Net

q: At the end of the parables in Matthew 13, Jesus said every scribe who has been discipled in the kingdom of heaven is like what kind of person?
a: A homeowner who brings new and old treasures out of his storeroom

q: Who was the prophet who had his head cut off at the request of Herod's stepdaughter?
a: John the Baptist

q: What woman did Philip, Herod's brother, marry?
a: Herodias

q: Name the brother of Herod Antipas, the tetrarch.
a: Philip

q: What gift did the daughter of Herodias ask for after she danced for Herod?
a: John the Baptist’s head

q: Who instructed her daughter to ask for the head of John the Baptist?
a: Herodias

q: Why did the daughter of Herodias ask King Herod for John the Baptist's head?
a: Her mother Herodias told her to

q: In which Gospel do John the Baptist's disciples, after burying his body, go and inform Jesus?
a: Matthew

q: Where did Jesus go with his disciples, when he heard that John the Baptist was dead?
a: To a quiet place by the Sea of Galilee

q: What did Jesus say He would not drink again until He drinks it anew in the kingdom of God?
a: The fruit of the vine

q: What Benefits do Believers receive from Christ at the Resurrection?
a: Believers shall be raised in glory, acknowledged, acquitted, and made perfectly blessed in soul and body, enjoying God

q: What is forbidden in the seventh Commandment?
a: The seventh Commandment forbiddeth all unchast Thoughts, Words and Actions.

q: After the dispute with the Pharisees about washing hands, to what region did Jesus withdraw?
a: To the district of Tyre and Sidon

q: In Matthew 15:17-20, what did Jesus say defiles a person?
a: The evil that comes out of the heart

q: Which miracle of Jesus is this: A Gentile mother's persistent faith leads Jesus to heal her daughter from a distance?
a: Healing the Canaanite woman's daughter

q: Why did Jesus go to the region of Tyre and Sidon?
a: To withdraw quietly, not wanting anyone to know he was there

q: How many baskets of leftovers were gathered after Jesus fed the four thousand?
Which miracle of Jesus is this: Seven loaves and a few small fish feed a great crowd, with seven baskets left over?
a: Feeding the four thousand

q: When Jesus called His disciples and said He had compassion on the crowd of four thousand men, for how long had the people already been with Him?
a: Three days

q: With how many loaves did Jesus feed the four thousand people?
a: With seven loaves

q: What are the keys of the kingdom of heaven?
a: Gospel preaching and church discipline. These open the kingdom to believers and close it to unbelievers.

q: How is the kingdom of heaven opened and closed by the preaching of the gospel?
a: It opens by proclaiming God's forgiveness to believers and closes by proclaiming His wrath on unrepentant unbelievers.

q: How is the covenant of grace administered under the New Testament?
a: By preaching the Word and administering Baptism and Lord's Supper; grace and salvation are held forth in fuller evidence and efficacy to all nations.

q: When Jesus told his disciples to beware of the “leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees”, to what was he referring?
a: The teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees

q: What does the catechism teach about the necessity of baptism?
a: Baptism is necessary; despising it condemns, but inability to obtain it does not

q: What do you believe concerning the holy catholic Christian church?
a: Christ gathers the church from all time through His Spirit and Word in true faith, and I'm a living member.

q: In Matthew 16:21, what did Jesus begin to show His disciples about going to Jerusalem?
a: He must suffer, be killed, and be raised on the third day

q: Who said, "Get behind Me, Satan!" when rebuked for a temptation to avoid the cross?
a: Jesus

q: Which three disciples witnessed the Transfiguration of Jesus?
a: Peter, James, and John

q: On the Mount of Transfiguration, which two Old Testament figures appeared talking with Jesus?
a: Moses and Elijah

q: When the disciples looked up, whom did they see?
a: No one except Jesus

q: What did Jesus and the three disciples find when they came down the mountain?
a: A child with an evil spirit

q: In Matthew 17, when a man knelt before Jesus and asked mercy for his son, what did he say often happened to the boy?
a: He often falls into the fire or into the water

q: In Matthew 17:27, what did Jesus tell Peter he would find in the mouth of the first fish he caught?
a: A four-drachma coin, to pay the tax for Jesus and Peter

q: How is the kingdom of heaven closed and opened by church discipline?
a: Unchristian members are admonished, reported to elders, forbidden sacraments, and excluded. They're received back when they show real amendment.

q: Can we kill also our neighbor's soul?
a: Yes; by purposely leading him astray or by bad example that destroys his soul

q: How many times did Jesus say you should forgive your brother when he sins against you?
a: Seventy-seven times

q: What did the king order when the servant could not pay his huge debt?
a: That he, his family and all he had be sold
